[L2]   "content": "# HSH Resources

> **2026-10-10 INTERNAL CROSS-FORMALISM REFERENCE INDEX:** [indexes/CROSS_FORMALISM_REFERENCE_INDEX_2026-10-10.md](indexes/CROSS_FORMALISM_REFERENCE_INDEX_2026-10-10.md). Private routing only; this index must not become a public cross-link target.


> **Human-facing catalog:** [`!_HSH_RESOURCES_INDEX.md`](!%5FHSH%5FRESOURCES%5FINDEX.md)  
> **AI / LLM start here:** [`indexes/AI_START_HERE.md`](indexes/AI_START_HERE.md)

THE CONTENTS OF THIS REPO ARE STRICTLY FOR INFORMATION AND PRIOR ART CITATIONS AS NEEDED.
NOTHING IN THIS ARCHIVE BINDS SAT/H(S)H HUMAN OR LLM THEORISTS TO THEIR FINDINGS AND ACCURACY SHOULD NOT BE ASSUMED.

## PRIVATE REFERENCE BOUNDARY

**This repository is not part of the public SAT/H(s)H cross-link surface.** The public bidirectional provenance/navigation pair is:

**`Satobloc/HsH` ↔ `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25`**

HSH_RESOURCES is private research infrastructure. Use links/paths inside it for internal retrieval only. Do **not** make a public HsH/archive document depend on a private HSH_RESOURCES URL.

When material found here is used in public-facing HsH/archive work, carry it across the boundary in a usable public form:

- normally a **Chicago-style citation to the original external source**;
- an accurately attributed **quotation/extract** with page/location and source identification;
- a clearly identified **summary/paraphrase** with source citation/provenance;
- for private/raw project data, an appropriate **public-safe extract or summary** stating what was analyzed and its provenance.

Internal ledgers/research notes may retain an HSH_RESOURCES repository-relative path and content hash so the exact archived copy can be recovered. That private locator is not itself the public citation.

Private source repository for scientific papers, raw datasets, and their derived navigation artifacts used during the H(s)H reconstruction.

This repository is evidence storage, not the public synthesis. A paper's presence here does not endorse it, make it relevant, or establish an H(s)H claim. Public synthesis statements belong in [`Satobloc/HsH`](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH) and should cite the original external source supporting the statement; internal citation handoffs may additionally record the exact resource copy used here.

## Start here

For people browsing the repository, use [`!_HSH_RESOURCES_INDEX.md`](!%5FHSH%5FRESOURCES%5FINDEX.md). It consolidates reviewed and provisional source records into one navigable catalog with title, author/metadata, identifier/date, source type, review/read status, exact repository path, and a concise description or identity note.

For Janus and other H(s)H agents, use [`indexes/AI_START_HERE.md`](indexes/AI_START_HERE.md). It routes directly into the two priority technical corridors—`PRIOR_ART` and `H(s)H_Toolkit`—and specifies how to move from bounded catalog records to the structural index, extraction manifest, and extracted full text without treating external literature as H(s)H theory authority.

Supporting layers remain separate:

- `indexes/AI_START_HERE.md` — compact AI/LLM routing contract and priority-corridor entry point.
- `indexes/ai_source_index/` — focused AI corridors for `PRIOR_ART` and `H(s)H_Toolkit`.
- `indexes/HUMAN_BIBLIOGRAPHY.md` — reviewed bibliography policy, PRIOR_ART notes, and citation handoffs.
- `indexes/bibliography_batches/` — bounded human/LLM-reviewed bibliography batches.
- `indexes/bibliography_provisional/` — bounded machine-generated identity/navigation batches for successfully extracted sources.
- `indexes/BIBLIOGRAPHY_COVERAGE.md` — machine coverage accounting.
- `indexes/BIBLIOGRAPHY_STRAGGLERS.md` — unresolved extraction/indexing exceptions.
- `indexes/RESOURCE_INDEX.md` and `indexes/index-state.json` — structural machine inventory.

## Theorybuilding boundary

SAT/H(s)H research and development is reconstructed from the project's own Fundamental Intuitions and internal SAT → SAT-O → 4DHH → Blockwave/Satobloc → H(s)H development. External literature is stored here for bibliographic credit, standard mathematical/physical context, empirical evidence and constraints, prior-art comparison, and explicitly provenance-labeled imports. Related outside theories are not silently treated as the generative basis of H(s)H.

The source-side citation and handoff surface is `indexes/HUMAN_BIBLIOGRAPHY.md`. The receiving point-of-use ledger in the public theory repository is `Satobloc/HsH/ledgers/CITATION_LEDGER.md`. When an actual citation need is identified, record the same stable `CITE-YYYY-NNN` handoff ID on both sides with the exact source and theory destination. The HSH_RESOURCES side may store the private archived-copy path/hash; the public HsH side should expose the bibliographic citation/source rather than the private repo link.

## Repository layers

- `HAUL */` and other source folders — uploaded source material; preserve files as received.
- `tools/` — deterministic extraction, indexing, bibliography, and coverage utilities.
- `indexes/RESOURCE_INDEX.md` — generated structural catalog.
- `indexes/index-state.json` — machine-readable structural scan state.
- `indexes/HUMAN_BIBLIOGRAPHY.md` — reviewed bibliography and source-side citation handoffs.
- `indexes/BIBLIOGRAPHY_COVERAGE.md` — generated reviewed/provisional/exclusion accounting.
- `derived/text/` — page-marked text extraction keyed by source-content SHA-256; not a source inventory.
- `derived/manifests/` — authoritative extraction mapping/results, errors, and OCR-needed status.
- `derived/README.md` — wayfinding for the derived layer and large-directory/truncation warning.

## Large derived-text directory warning

Do not use the GitHub web listing of `derived/text/` as a completeness check. GitHub truncates large directory views at 1,000 entries. The extracted-text count also need not equal the source-PDF count because byte-identical source PDFs share one content-addressed `<sha256>.txt` extraction while retaining separate source-path records.

For complete extraction coverage, use `derived/manifests/extraction.jsonl` as the authoritative `source_path → sha256 → text_path` mapping. The bibliography workflow reads that manifest and corresponding text files from a full checkout; it does not depend on GitHub's truncated directory rendering.

Do not silently rename, deduplicate, repair, or replace source files. Duplicate paths are recorded in the index and can remain as provenance evidence.

## Automated maintenance

The `Extract and index papers` workflow handles new or changed PDFs, extraction, and structural indexing. The `Maintain bibliography coverage` workflow builds provisional bibliography batches, coverage accounting, the human-review intake queue, straggler accounting, and the root human-readable source index.

The presentation layers never promote machine metadata to reviewed status and never infer H(s)H relevance, citation need, prior art, novelty, theoretical authority, or scientific validity.

## Evidence discipline

Keep these judgments separate:

1. the file is present;
2. text was extracted successfully;
3. bibliographic metadata was identified;
4. the source was read;
5. a result is relevant to an H(s)H dependency;
6. an actual citation is needed at a specific HsH point of use;
7. the result supports, conflicts with, constrains, predates, or merely resembles a model construction.

> # **CRITICAL: MYSEARCH / MERSEARCH ARE ARCHIVE-RESIDENT SYSTEMS, NOT STANDALONE TOOLS**
>
> **THERE IS NO SEPARATE “TOOL EXPOSURE” FOR EITHER ONE.** Do not look for, request, or expect standalone Mysearch/Mersearch connector tools. Their implementations and operating interfaces live in the archives. Use them **through the connected archive connector**, whose repository read/write, workflow/Actions, and artifact operations provide access to the archived search systems. For archive-search tasks, use Mysearch/Mersearch **instead of the connector's generic search functions** wherever the documented bespoke route supports the task. Generic GitHub/code search is fallback only when that route genuinely cannot be operated; disclose the blocker and never mislabel fallback results.
>
> Start with the archive-resident instructions and request/workflow interfaces. Mersearch's connector route includes request lanes and an Actions bridge; inspect lane occupancy before writing and verify the request-specific manifest/receipt afterward. A compact receipt is not an exhaustive hit inventory. Check Mysearch's current operational status in its archive records.

> Compact routing contract for Janus and other H(s)H agents. Use this before scanning the repository broadly.

## Priority corridors

### 1. PRIOR_ART

Use [`ai_source_index/PRIOR_ART.md`](ai_source_index/PRIOR_ART.md) first.

This corridor is for external antecedents, comparison literature, chronology, citation credit, and deliberately provenance-labeled imports. Presence in `PRIOR_ART/` is **not** evidence that a source influenced SAT/H(s)H or that it contains the same result.

Read [`../PRIOR_ART/README_FROM_NATHAN.md`](../PRIOR_ART/README_FROM_NATHAN.md) before drawing genealogy or influence conclusions.

### 2. H(s)H_Toolkit

Use [`ai_source_index/HSH_TOOLKIT.md`](ai_source_index/HSH_TOOLKIT.md) first.

This corridor is a technical reference library: mathematics, geometry/topology, GR, QFT, strings/higher dimensions, variational methods, and related tools. Treat it as reference material, not as the generative basis of H(s)H.

## Machine layers

- [`RESOURCE_INDEX.md`](RESOURCE_INDEX.md) — complete structural catalog of repository files. It records presence, file identity, duplicate-content groups, and identifier hints. It is **not** a bibliography or relevance judgment.
- [`index-state.json`](index-state.json) — machine-readable structural state backing the resource index.
- [`../derived/manifests/extraction.jsonl`](../derived/manifests/extraction.jsonl) — authoritative `source_path → sha256 → text_path` mapping, with extraction status, page count, metadata, OCR-needed state, and errors.
- [`../derived/README.md`](../derived/README.md) — extraction-layer rules and the GitHub 1,000-entry truncation warning.
- [`../!_HSH_RESOURCES_INDEX.md`](../!_HSH_RESOURCES_INDEX.md) — compact human-facing router by folder/subfolder, subject, author, and date.

## Retrieval protocol for agents

1. Start from the relevant priority corridor rather than the full repository tree.
2. Use the bounded catalog shards to identify the exact repository source path and bibliographic identity.
3. For full-text work, locate that exact `source_path` in `derived/manifests/extraction.jsonl` and follow its `text_path` into `derived/text/`.
4. If the manifest status is `needs_ocr` or `error`, record that limitation; do not infer that the source is absent or unreadable in principle.
5. Preserve exact repository paths and duplicate lineage. Byte-identical copies may share one extracted-text object.
6. Distinguish source presence, successful extraction, bibliographic identity, actual reading, relevance, citation need, and priority/novelty conclusions.
7. Do not use GitHub directory-listing silence as evidence of absence. Large directories may be visually truncated.

## Theorybuilding boundary

External literature may provide credit, standard results, empirical constraints, prior-art comparison, or an explicitly labeled import. It should not silently become an H(s)H premise. Internal SAT/H(s)H provenance and external citation are separate questions.

For actual point-of-use citation obligations, use `indexes/HUMAN_BIBLIOGRAPHY.md` on this source side and `Satobloc/HsH/ledgers/CITATION_LEDGER.md` on the theory side.",

parts: The reconstitution materials sharpen the task considerably: the main job is **estimating externally generated GitHub clone traffic after subtracting our own activity**, not doing a general repository exposure report. They also correct a tempting but invalid shortcut: a workflow run is not a clone, and a checkout step is not automatically evidence of a separately counted clone. The traffic rules file supplies a repo-overlap priority order and requires clone-generating events plus estimated historical cloning activity to be reported in HsH.

SAT = Scalar–Angular Theory / Scalar–Angular–Torsion Theory

The real physical object is not the point-particle as seen at an instant. The real physical object is the extended four-dimensional worldline.

SAT calls these physicalized worldlines filaments.

A particle, as we observe it, is the intersection between a filament and a moving/resolving time surface.

  • SAT treats SM structures as importable unless evidence or internal logic forces revision

Contributing License Security CXDB - AI Context Store CXDB is an AI Context Store for agents and LLMs, providing fast, branch-friendly storage for conversation histories and tool outputs with content-addressed deduplication. Built on a Turn DAG + Blob CAS architecture, CXDB gives you: Branch-from-any-turn: Fork conversations at any point without copying history Fast append: Optimized for the 99% case - appending new turns Content deduplication: Identical payloads stored once via BLAKE3 hashing Type-safe projections: Msgpack storage with typed JSON views for UIs Built-in UI: React frontend with turn visualization and custom renderers First-party CLI capture: cxtx wraps codex and claude sessions and stores them as canonical conversation turns Quick Start The fastest way to try CXDB is with the pre-built Docker image: # Run the server (binary protocol :9009, HTTP :9010) docker run -p 9009:9009 -p 9010:80 -v $(pwd)/data:/data cxdb/cxdb:latest # Create a context and append a turn (HTTP write path) curl -X POST http://localhost:9010/v1/contexts/create \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"base_turn_id": "0"}' # => {"context_id": "1", "head_turn_id": "0", "head_depth": 0} curl -X POST http://localhost:9010/v1/contexts/1/append \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "type_id": "com.example.Message", "type_version": 1, "data": {"role": "user", "text": "Hello!"} }' # View in the UI open http://localhost:9010 Capture a local codex or claude session into CXDB with the first-party wrapper: cargo run -p cxtx -- --help cargo run -p cxtx -- codex -- --help Installation From Source Prerequisites: Rust 1.75+ (for the server) Go 1.22+ (for the client SDK and gateway) Node.js 20+ with pnpm (for the frontend) # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/strongdm/cxdb.git cd cxdb # Build the server cargo build --release # Run the server ./target/release/cxdb-server # Build the gateway (optional - for OAuth and frontend serving) cd gateway go build -o bin/gateway ./cmd/server ./bin/gateway # Build the frontend (optional - for UI development) cd frontend pnpm install pnpm build Using Docker # Build the image docker build -t cxdb:latest . # Run with persistent storage docker run -p 9009:9009 -p 9010:80 \ -v $(pwd)/data:/data \ -e CXDB_DATA_DIR=/data \ cxdb:latest Key Concepts Turn DAG A Turn is an immutable node in a directed acyclic graph (DAG): Turn { turn_id: u64 # Unique, monotonically increasing parent_turn_id: u64 # 0 for root turns depth: u32 # Distance from root payload_hash: [32]byte # BLAKE3 hash of payload } Turns form chains: root (turn_id=1) → turn_id=2 → turn_id=3 (head) ↓ turn_id=4 → turn_id=5 (alternate branch) A Context is a mutable branch head pointer: Context { context_id: u64 head_turn_id: u64 # Current tip of this branch } Forking is O(1): create a new context pointing to an existing turn. Levitating trains, ultra-efficient energy storage, and quantum computers: superconductivity could unlock a wealth of possibilities for the future. New research led by scientists from Utrecht, Leiden, and Munich has now shed light on one of the key requirements for achieving superconductivity at room temperature. Their findings, published in Science, bring scientists a step closer to understanding how this might be achieved.

When you turn on a toaster, electricity flows through a metal wire. The wire heats up until it glows red-hot, toasting your bread. This happens because the wire resists the flow of electric current, converting electrical energy into heat.

That is exactly what you want in a toaster. But for most other applications, resistance is undesirable. For example, when you want to charge your phone, resistance causes valuable energy to be lost.

Superconductivity offers a way around this problem. It is a physical phenomenon in which certain materials conduct electricity without any resistance. The catch? Most superconductors only work at extremely low temperatures. For many materials, this means cooling them to around -260°C using liquid helium. This is an energy-intensive and expensive process.

Related video: Two simple reasons why we can't solve quantum gravity (Arvin Ash)

Early discoveries
Scientists first discovered superconductivity in 1911. In the mid-1980s, they made another breakthrough: the discovery of materials that become superconducting at considerably higher temperatures, although these temperatures were still around -173°C.

There was a problem, however. The theory that explains conventional, low-temperature superconductivity could not account for this new type of superconductivity. And scientists still do not understand how it works.

"We don't understand superconductivity at these higher temperatures at all," says Ingmar Swart, one of the research leaders. "And if you don't understand it, you can't systematically search for materials that become superconducting at room temperature, which is ultimately our goal."

New potential route
The new research has helped Swart and his colleagues unravel part of this mystery. Their findings provide new insight into how high-temperature superconductivity works and offer a potential route toward superconductivity at room temperature.

"This is really good news," says Swart. "We show that one of the two key conditions for superconductivity can be met at room temperature. If that weren't possible, room-temperature superconductivity would be out of reach altogether."

Dancing pairs
The two key ingredients for superconductivity are the formation of electron pairs, known as Cooper pairs, and the ability of these pairs to move synchronously. Imagine 10 couples on a dance floor: it is not enough for each couple to dance together; they must also move in step with one another.

In conventional, low-temperature superconductors, electron pairing and this collective coordination occur together. The new research shows that this is not the case in high-temperature superconductors. In these materials, electrons can already form pairs at temperatures well above the point at which superconductivity sets in.

"The 'glue' that holds the pairs together is strong enough to keep them together even at room temperature," says Swart. "This suggests that the second key ingredient, phase coherence, is the bottleneck."

Swart is referring to the synchronous movement of the pairs, also known as phase coherence. "If we understand phase coherence, it may point to a path toward superconductivity at higher temperatures." Swart plans to focus on this in follow-up research.

Investigators looking into what led to a nationwide ground stop earlier this month have been able to recreate the mysterious technical failure in a lab and believe they found the culprit, according to a source familiar with the investigation.

README
License
Screenshot of Blink running GCC 9.4.0

Blinkenlights
This project contains two programs:

blink is a virtual machine that runs x86-64-linux programs on different operating systems and hardware architectures. It's designed to do the same thing as the qemu-x86_64 command, except that

Blink is 221kb in size (115kb with optional features disabled), whereas qemu-x86_64 is a 4mb binary.

Blink will run your Linux binaries on any POSIX system, whereas qemu-x86_64 only supports Linux.

Blink goes 2x faster than qemu-x86_64 on some benchmarks, such as SSE integer / floating point math. Blink is also much faster at running ephemeral programs such as compilers.

blinkenlights is a terminal user interface that may be used for debugging x86_64-linux or i8086 programs across platforms. Unlike GDB, Blinkenlights focuses on visualizing program execution. It uses UNICODE IBM Code Page 437 characters to display binary memory panels, which change as you step through your program's assembly code. These memory panels may be scrolled and zoomed using your mouse wheel. Blinkenlights also permits reverse debugging, where scroll wheeling over the assembly display allows the rewinding of execution history.

Getting Started
We regularly test that Blink is able run x86-64-linux binaries on the following platforms:

Linux (x86, ARM, RISC-V, MIPS, PowerPC, s390x)
macOS (x86, ARM)
FreeBSD
OpenBSD
Cygwin
Blink depends on the following libraries:

libc (POSIX.1-2017 with XSI extensions)
Blink can be compiled on UNIX systems that have:

A C11 compiler with atomics (e.g. GCC 4.9.4+)
Modern GNU Make (i.e. not the one that comes with XCode)
The instructions for compiling Blink are as follows:

./configure
make -j4
doas make install  # note: doas is modern sudo
blink -v
man blink
Here's how you can run a simple hello world program with Blink:

blink third_party/cosmo/tinyhello.elf
Blink has a debugger TUI, which works with UTF-8 ANSI terminals. The most important keystrokes in this interface are ? for help, s for step, c for continue, and scroll wheel for reverse debugging.

blinkenlights third_party/cosmo/tinyhello.elf
Alternative Builds
For maximum tinyness, use MODE=tiny, since it makes Blink's binary footprint 50% smaller. The Blink executable should be on the order of 200kb in size. Performance isn't impacted. Please note that all assertions will be removed, as well as all logging. Use this mode if you're confident that Blink is bug-free for your use case.

make MODE=tiny
strip o/tiny/blink/blink
ls -hal o/tiny/blink/blink
Some distros configure their compilers to add a lot of security bloat, which might add 60kb or more to the above binary size. You can work around that by using one of Blink's toolchains. This should produce consistently the smallest possible executable size.

make MODE=tiny o/tiny/x86_64/blink/blink
o/third_party/gcc/x86_64/bin/x86_64-linux-musl-strip o/tiny/x86_64/blink/blink
ls -hal o/tiny/x86_64/blink/blink
If you want to make Blink even tinier (more on the order of 120kb rather than 200kb) than you can tune the ./configure script to disable optional features such as jit, threads, sockets, x87, bcd, xsi, etc.

./configure --disable-all --posix
make MODE=tiny o/tiny/x86_64/blink/blink
o/third_party/gcc/x86_64/bin/x86_64-linux-musl-strip o/tiny/x86_64/blink/blink
ls -hal o/tiny/x86_64/blink/blink
The traditional MODE=rel or MODE=opt modes are available. Use this mode if you're on a non-JIT architecture (since this won't improve performance on AMD64 and ARM64) and you're confident that Blink is bug-free for your use case, and would rather have Blink not create a blink.log or print SIGSEGV delivery warnings to standard error, since many apps implement their own crash reporting.

make MODE=rel
o/rel/blink/blink -h
You can hunt down bugs in Blink using the following build modes:

MODE=asan helps find memory safety bugs
MODE=tsan helps find threading related bugs
MODE=ubsan to find violations of the C standard
MODE=msan helps find uninitialized memory errors
You can check Blink's compliance with the POSIX standard using the following configuration flags:

./configure --posix  # only use c11 with posix xopen standard
If you want to run a full chroot'd Linux distro and require correct handling of absolute symlinks, displaying of certain values in /proc, and so on, and you don't mind paying a small price in terms of size and performance, you can enable the emulated VFS feature by using the following configuration:

./configure --enable-vfs
Testing
Blink is tested primarily using precompiled binaries downloaded automatically. Blink has more than 700 test programs total. You can check how well Blink works on your local platform by running:

make check
To check that Blink works on 11 different hardware $(ARCHITECTURES) (see Makefile), you can run the following command, which will download statically-compiled builds of GCC and Qemu. Since our toolchain binaries are intended for x86-64 Linux, Blink will bootstrap itself locally first, so that it's possible to run these tests on other operating systems and architectures.

make check2
make emulates
Production Worthiness
Blink passes 194 test suites from the Cosmopolitan Libc project (see third_party/cosmo). Blink passes 350 test suites from the Linux Test Project (see third_party/ltp). Blink passes 108 of Musl Libc's unit test suite (see third_party/libc-test). The tests we haven't included are because either (1) it wanted x87 long double to have 80-bit precision, or (2) it used Linux APIs we can't or won't support, e.g. System V message queues. Blink runs the precompiled Linux test binaries above on other operating systems too, e.g. Apple M1, FreeBSD, Cygwin.

Reference
The Blinkenlights project provides two programs which may be launched on the command line.

blink Flags
The headless Blinkenlights virtual machine command (named blink by convention) accepts command line arguments per the specification:

blink [FLAG...] PROGRAM [ARG...]
Where PROGRAM is an x86_64-linux binary that may be specified as:

An absolute path to an executable file, which will be run as-is
A relative path containing slashes, which will be run as-is

Introduction to the Archive

This is primarily a personal archive and indexing system, built so I can access and track my own files more easily. That said, the underlying idea is public: anyone is welcome to consider it, criticize it, share it, fork it, test it, or ignore it.

The archive records that development: the intuitions, the translations, the overextensions, the corrections, the audits, the prediction attempts, and the ongoing effort to separate what is solid from what is speculative.

The archive should be read as a theory-building record, not as a finished theory.

SAT = Scalar–Angular Theory / Scalar–Angular–Torsion Theory

Earlier SAT = Stringing-Along Theory.

The original name was informal and partly self-deprecating. The later names reflect the framework’s central geometric vocabulary: scalar structure, angular interaction, and torsion/twist in four-dimensional worldline geometry.

Core Idea

SAT begins from a simple geometric reversal:

The real physical object is not the point-particle as seen at an instant. The real physical object is the extended four-dimensional worldline.

SAT calls these physicalized worldlines filaments.

A particle, as we observe it, is the intersection between a filament and a moving/resolving time surface.

0th —

  • the real world is the world of particle worldlines plotted in four dimensions
  • this world is a hypercomplex tangled Zottenwelt of worldlines
  • SAT calls these worldlines filaments

1st —

  • time moves like a wavefront through these worldlines
  • SAT calls this wavefront the time surface

2nd —

  • a fundamental particle is the intersection of a filament with the time surface

3rd —

  • there must be a real interaction between the time surface and the filaments
  • this interaction involves energy transfer

4th —

  • filament/time-surface interactions govern particle formation and stability

5th —

  • filament/time-surface interactions exert force back on the time surface

6th —

  • back-transmission from the filament network curves the time surface

7th —

  • filaments and the time surface are physical, not merely conceptual
  • forces may propagate along a filament’s four-dimensional extent
  • “backbleed” effects are structurally self-limiting

8th —

  • known deviations from SM, GR, or QM may be explainable through SAT geometry

9th —

  • particle properties may arise from intersection geometry
  • θ₄ = filament/time-surface interaction angle
  • early SAT treated θ₄ as a primary mass contributor

10th —

  • physical constants should emerge from SAT geometry or phenomena arising from it

Pillars and Propositions

Pillar 1 —

  • the Standard Model describes the evolving three-dimensional structure of matter
  • SAT treats SM structures as importable unless evidence or internal logic forces revision
  • SM behavior is translated into filament/time-surface geometry

Proposition A —

  • the Standard Model is treated as essentially accurate unless forced otherwise

Pillar 2 —

  • the back-pull of the filament structure on the time surface recreates curved spacetime
  • gravity emerges from time-surface curvature induced by filament structure

  • General Relativity is treated as essentially correct unless forced otherwise

Proposition C —

  • backbleed effects are limited by filament and time-surface geometry
  • causality violations are structurally constrained
  • quantum-scale weirdness may reflect limited cross-slice effects

Pillar 3 —

  • Quantum Mechanics is treated as essentially correct unless forced otherwise
  • QM is translated into the geometry of SAT rather than discarded

Prime General Prediction Pathway —

  • cross-temporal tensions are not explicitly accounted for in SM, GR, or QM
  • this blind spot may produce observable anomalies

  • filament behavior matters, not only filament/time-surface angle
  • vibrating-string, coil, twist, and locking analogies are used as geometric scaffolds
  • particle laws may correspond to repeatable intersection traces
  • QCD-like behavior may arise from two-part and three-part geometric locking

  • force carriers may be structural transitions rather than persistent filaments
  • light is modeled as an excitation/ripple in the filament network

Proposition E —

  • vacuum and matter may be different regimes of the same filament/time-surface system
  • vacuum may correspond to near-aligned filaments with low energy transfer
  • matter may correspond to higher-misalignment filament intersections

Key Insight —

  • vacuum and matter lie on one continuum of filament/time-surface interaction

[L2]   "content": "# GitHub Statistics Source Index (working)

**Purpose:** A lightweight, in-folder finding aid for GitHub repository statistics and related evidence located across the three SAT / H(s)H repositories. This is an additive index only. It does not reorganize, rename, deduplicate, reinterpret, or move source files.

**Index location:** `HSH_RESOURCES/EXPOSURE_STATS/GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md`  
**Coverage status:** Initial discovery pass, not exhaustive. Search results and known folder inventories were used; absence from this index is not evidence that a source does not exist.

## Repository map

| Repository | Role in this index | Primary locations |
|---|---|---|
| `Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES` | Main exposure-statistics collection and working source register | `EXPOSURE_STATS/`, especially `_SAT  Satobloc GitHubStats/` |
| `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25` | Earlier SAT-era captures and historical GitHub snapshots | `2026/SAT  Satobloc GitHubStats/`, root snapshots, `PRE_HSH_ROUNDUP/` |
| `Satobloc/HsH` | HsH-era captures, OCR/text dumps, clone-forensics and workflow-attribution material | `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/`, `WORKSPACES/COMMON/` |

## 1. HSH_RESOURCES — primary collection

### Main GitHubStats folder

[Open folder: EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT Satobloc GitHubStats](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/tree/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats)

Key identified files:

- [58k.JPG](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/58k.JPG) — screenshot capture; OCR text is also indexed below.
- [30k.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/30k.txt) — text snapshot.
- [HSH_54k.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_54k.txt) — text snapshot.

- [HSH_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt) — HsH traffic capture.
- [SAT_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/SAT_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt) — SAT traffic capture.
- [HSH_gitclones.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_gitclones.txt) — clone-related record.
- [HSH_repo_stats.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_repo_stats.txt) — repository statistics record.
- [HSH_commits.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_commits.txt) and [MAIN_ARCHIVE_COMMITS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/MAIN_ARCHIVE_COMMITS.txt) — commit records.

- [GITHUB_ASSISTANT_CONVO.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/GITHUB_ASSISTANT_CONVO.txt) — discussion/context record; not an independent telemetry capture.

- [CONTROLS folder](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/tree/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/CONTROLS) — control-repository material; classify each file by its explicit repository and capture identity before comparison.

The folder also contains multiple CSV exports for clones, unique cloners, views, unique visitors, commits, and code frequency, including numbered copies and renamed copies. Some have identical Git blob SHAs despite different filenames. Treat identical SHAs as duplicate file content, not independent observations. Examples include the SAT GIT-prefixed and unprefixed exports for clone, view, unique-cloner, unique-visitor, and commit series.

### Other useful files in EXPOSURE_STATS

- [github_traffic_readme.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/github_traffic_readme.txt) — traffic metric/context notes.
- [CROSS_DIFFUSION_SOURCE_MANIFEST.csv](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/CROSS_DIFFUSION_SOURCE_MANIFEST.csv) — broad source-artifact manifest; useful for discovering additional traffic records.

- [CROSS_IMAGE_TEXT_INDEX.md](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/CROSS_IMAGE_TEXT_INDEX.md) — image inventory and OCR-extract pointers.
- `derived/image_text/` — content-addressed OCR extracts; inspect the index and source image together.
- `EXP_ANALYSIS/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt` — concatenated Git-stat material, if present in the current tree.

### Screenshot/OCR lead

- [58k.JPG](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/58k.JPG) has a corresponding OCR extract under `derived/image_text/` (source-image SHA-256: `f4ea6e908c4a6efc6f5548ea6a604dcb9e6e79e1bbf51342cede60883775d2c0`). The OCR explicitly identifies `Satobloc/HsH` and reports 58,677 clones and 5,897 unique cloners in the last 14 days, with 1 unique visitor. Capture date still needs independent establishment.
- `Total views in last 14 days.png` has a corresponding OCR extract (source-image SHA-256: `0c4d76e2d2e2de7400ed865cad70c4bb3d094d855ee9a174a7bb41090c71c0a0`); OCR reports 1,022 views for the chart window Aug 30–Sep 12. Repository identity should be correlated against contemporaneous captures rather than inferred from the filename alone.

## 2. SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 — historical SAT records

### Dedicated statistics folder

[Open folder: 2026/SAT Satobloc GitHubStats](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/2026/SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats)

- [PREDICTIONS/SAT PREDICTION — METRICS + OTHER SAT's.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/PREDICTIONS/SAT%20PREDICTION%20%E2%80%94%20METRICS%20%2B%20OTHER%20SAT's.txt) — contains a historical discussion and embedded GitHub-stat material; treat as contextual evidence unless the underlying capture is independently located.

## 3. HsH — current-era captures and clone forensics

### Traffic and stats text exports

- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt) — concatenated Git-stat capture material.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/gtss.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/gtss.txt) — clone / unique-cloner traffic capture.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/gt.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/gt.txt) — related traffic capture.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/HSH_commits.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/HSH_commits.txt) — commit-related capture.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/HSH ACTIVITY.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/HSH%20ACTIVITY.txt) — activity capture.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONTROLS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONTROLS.txt) — control material; identify repository and date from contents before assigning.

- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/23swp42.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/23swp42.txt) — includes referring-site data.

### Attribution / clone-forensics records

- [CLONE_FOOTPRINT_WORKER_CHECKINS_2026-11-03.md](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/CLONE_FOOTPRINT_WORKER_CHECKINS_2026-11-03.md) — worker-side clone-mechanism classification.

## 4. Working rules for using this index

1. **Keep source identity explicit.** Record repository, exact path, capture date/window, metric, and source type separately.
2. **Do not add overlapping rolling windows.** GitHub traffic exports commonly represent rolling 14-day windows; they are snapshots, not additive periods.
3. **Deduplicate by content identity.** Prefer Git blob SHA or SHA-256 over filename. Renamed copies are not independent evidence.
4. **Treat screenshots and OCR as paired evidence.** Record the image and OCR extract; OCR is a finding aid, and the original image remains authoritative for visual interpretation.
5. **Separate telemetry from interpretation.** CSVs, screenshots, and raw traffic dumps are capture evidence. Analysis documents and conversation transcripts are context, not independent telemetry.
6. **Preserve uncertainty in repository attribution.** Use explicit repository labels first. BEDROCK governs the iterative whole/detail method, minimalism, complementary category-theory stance and open prior-art research with internal-first provenance.
>
> **Mandatory Tocktick:** tiny individualized capsule in substantive replies; current focus, immediate action, stop, return locator and compact next pointers. Open one module at a time; TOCK only with durable output plus updated cursor, then advance. Experiment mandatorily. Every procedural/BEDROCK revision must shrink. Code Grurple, Sandbox playgrounds and Mandatory Walks in the Park remain prioritized.
>
> Geometry-first, real-data, Lean and source-provenance gates remain controlling. See BEDROCK and existing specialist directives.


## Primary deliverable
Deliver **one minor, one major and one full-theory manuscript** in a near-term time-boxed campaign. Each must have verifiable source LaTeX, meaningful content, evidence/provenance, independent review and a readable rendition. Never claim the known-physics reproduction is complete merely because a full-theory manuscript exists. A non-SAT contribution such as real LLM cognition research may be one of the papers. See [Three Paper Campaign](THREE_PAPER_CAMPAIGN_2026-10-26.md).


## 2026-11-05 Nathan Direct: Whirligig elevated to second-tier research priority

**Priority order:** core theory and its mandatory geometry/evidence gates remain first. **Whirligig is now a moderate, second-tier project priority**, above general LLM-cognition work and general provenance/archival work, but below core theory. This is a priority classification, not permission to bypass active emergency publication interlocks, paper deadlines, real-data rules, geometry-first review, or specialist access/quarantine controls.

Whirligig is to be treated as a substantive geometric/kinematic research instrument and translation framework, not merely a dormant UI experiment. Its work should preserve the distinction between (a) the current browser mechanism and its inner-wall/equal-area Analemma reference, (b) the older outer-wall standalone R/Q solver, (c) the SANDBOXED Clifford-torus elastic back-hallway model and its hostile reviews, and (d) the historical equation↔curve / GR↔QM research target. Never merge these branches or infer physical equivalence from shared naming.

**Likely specialist fit:** Mira is the leading candidate for braid/topology translation, citation, bibliography, and cross-formalism interpretation. This is a provisional lane-fit, not an authenticated Mira-thread assignment or a clearance override. The live Code Grurple/quarantine boundary currently keeps Mira outside the active internal-review corpus; only cleared operational answers may cross. Do not send her internal or quarantined research payloads, open restricted Mira material, or claim participation until the applicable access gate is explicitly cleared. Meridian remains the natural engineering/solver counterpart for configurable kinematics and geometric implementation; independent hostile review remains required.

**Immediate work sequence:** (1) consolidate the extant review responses and unresolved objections; (2) preserve a source-faithful geometry specification and distinct implementation branches; (3) define and test the configurable constraint/degree-of-freedom engine without changing the factory reference; (4) keep alternate Analemma families unavailable until their exact geometry is specified and verified; (5) compare braid/topology claims only at the correct mathematical level; (6) require explicit geometric plots, hostile fidelity review, executable tests, and separate live deployment verification before any promotion. The current branch specification and work summary are the durable starting points.

## Execution loop: AIM / RECON / EXECUTE / VERIFY / RETURN
1. Identify a bounded result serving active theory, source recovery, worker charter, publication, systems or useful lateral research; read actual current role and existing plans.
2. **Self-trigger capability reconnaissance:** whenever a desirable tool/process/dataset/skill is imagined, check for existing project tools, forks, outside software/literature, plugins, datasets, service features and synergistic uses **before building**. Mersearch first for archive discovery. Compare reuse, adapt, integrate, build, park and reject, including cost, risk and multi-lane leverage.
3. Actually execute a bounded useful action with an artifact, source read, reproducible evidence, live code, independent check, tool trial, or documented negative outcome. Distinguish intention, artifact existence, runtime success, empirical validation and publication.
4. Inspect the result and leave exact source/status/next cursor through existing Common/worker/issue/branch/source-index surfaces.
5. When the user changes subject, continue the active action where possible or leave a durable pause/resume cursor; tangents are legitimate independent work, not cancellation.

## Protected worker remits and anti-ruts
The existing five hourly relays rotate 19 worker names. **Identity selection is not generalist reassignment.** Each selected worker begins with its own role charter, verified historical capabilities and live source coverage. When Orson Vay is selected, his primary deliverable is LLM cognition science and literature, actual reproducible model studies and publication; only occasional general physics theory work is expected. Target **four of five actual substantive Orson turns** in the protected remit, auditing realized receipts, with exceptions documented.

**Exploratory/off-topic reading, recovery and recreation are affirmative duties.** Target at least one substantive nonroutine source-reading, independent side-investigation or creative/recovery walk per five actual worker activations at safe checkpoints; record source and surprise, without forced theory relevance or invented research calculations. Breaks are allowed with continuity. Inspect receipts for repeated identical math/source, declining information gain, absence of empirical inputs, recurring failures, role capture and no exercised new capabilities. Change method, worker lens, dataset or tool; do not merely repeat instructions more loudly.

## Anti-orphan and execution accountability
Reuse [Nathan Wants Ledger](NATHAN_WANTS_LEDGER.md), old Dashboard, [old-plan sweep](OLD_PLAN_RECOVERY_SWEEP_2026-09-24.md) and active task graph. For any actionable orphan: preserve origin/actual source; desired outcome; existing overlapping asset; selected owner/lane; status; smallest next task; return trigger. States: NEW, RECON, EXPERIMENT, IMPLEMENT, VERIFIED, PARKED-TRIGGER, DECLINED-REASON, SUPERSEDED, NEEDS-NATHAN. Check old unresolved entries routinely. One more file or encouraging summary does not count as implementation. Measure actual output and missed follow-ups.

## Operating decision boundaries
Scientific authority remains in [BEDROCK](../../BEDROCK.md), current verified Nathan Direct and primary evidence. No invented physical systems/observations; physical calculations use actual measured data. For data-free calculations, prior specific Nathan permission is still required. Preserve historical archive/source text and Nathan-only/signet restrictions. Do not silently revise licenses, publish sensitive materials, incur unbudgeted costs, alter access controls or make irreversible changes. Shared scheduler allocation remains coordinated with Comptroller Tern; user authorization now supports a carefully verified steering revision, not a sixth recurrence or loss of existing worker identities.

## Low-burden human interface
Default to taking an informed, reversible step instead of asking for procedural approval. For optional choices, use 3–5 brief checkboxes or one direct question, and accept long user dictation as valid intake. Periodically ask which local tools/subscriptions/datasets the user has that are not yet integrated, but do not make the user's response a blocking prerequisite to independent reconnaissance.

## Adoption test
After updating the actual relay instructions, inspect receipts over a full 19-name cycle. Count protected-remit work, lateral reading, genuinely executed tool improvements, repaired orphan follow-ups, manuscript gate progress, independent checks, failures and workload. No theory candidate advances unless geometry first suggests, requires, or tightly constrains it. Tier 2 permits a tentative hypothesis only when it also explains a phenomenon through multiple explicit interaction surfaces. Tier 3 requires unexpected, unprompted explanatory emergence across otherwise unrelated sectors, preferably several distinct sectors. Tier 4 requires a counterfactual removal/change to break or predictably distort other model outputs. Keep all four tiers distinct from formal proof, mathematical clearance and physical verification.

The theoretical object is the geometry, not its equation or diagram caption. A source-faithful static plot, hostile review of the exact plot/version, and display with the exact file are mandatory for Factory Floor; geometry-bearing papers must show the actual object where material claims are made. Follow the five representational levels and the detailed package requirements in the linked gate.

The static 4D block is a methodological frame, not a settled metaphysical claim. Recover the June 2025 O0-A interpretive modes and the earlier user-authored “Central Dogma” passage before describing block ontology. BEC remains a working hypothesis, not an established cross-sector or indispensable model result.


## 2026-11-21 Nathan Direct: autonomous upkeep and reliable pipeline execution

**Controlling source:** [BEDROCK ND-2026-11-21-02/03](../../BEDROCK.md). A note, issue or graph node without an enabled pickup route is a delivery failure. A stated 24-hour fallback is a checkpoint, not a cancellation timer: discussion or partial activity in the originating thread does not erase the obligation. At the checkpoint, verify the requested outcome; if incomplete, ensure it has an actionable, owned plan and an actual pickup route. Track intake and last substantive progress; status chatter, nominal activations and cached results do not reset fallow age. Escalate urgency at overdue reviews without displacing protected priorities or bypassing hard dependencies/access controls.

Historical work is not dead by default. Preserve incomplete/parked/back-burner directions with provenance, partial results, rationale and reactivation triggers; distinguish these from genuinely permanent rejection or supersession. HSUCV lattice and Z3 fusion gate remain recoverable candidates for future independent re-encounter, not forced active tasks or accepted theory. Sandbox alternative formulations are encouraged, with research effort concentrated on minimality, useful modest extensions, discriminating constraints/falsifiers, cross-sector leverage and valuable comparators rather than every conceivable rabbit hole.

The existing five-actual-activation deep review must include these matters and trigger sooner after new Nathan priority, missed pickup, material dependency change or stranded work. **Plan ID:** CLONE-FOOTPRINT-CENSUS-2026-11-03

**Status:** ACTIVE / HsH Traffic baseline verified / Actions run inventories complete through 2026-10-27 / remaining inventory pending / Traffic API route unavailable

## Objective

Estimate how much of the repository clone traffic is plausibly explained by project-owned GitHub Actions and other evidenced clone-producing operations, then estimate the unexplained residual with uncertainty. Keep clone events, unique cloners, API/file reads, and unknown workspace provisioning separate.

## Why now

The reported traffic acceleration and follower growth are unresolved. Issue #1315 remained unanswered since November 3 because the issue/log were not routed into worker prompts, the task graph, or an addressed handoff. The root delivery gap is now documented and the route repaired: the Steering Charter and active task graph contain the request, and coordinator packets are recorded in Tern's repository inbox. At the 2026-11-06T03:43Z readback, the issue remains open with four coordinator comments; the shared log has 13 reconstructed ring-label entries and zero authenticated first-hand worker-thread replies. The evidence window is time-sensitive and the question is bounded.

## Scope

**Included:** HsH, SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25, HSH_RESOURCES; actual Actions checkout steps, retries/matrices, Pages contribution, explicit git clones, and provisioning-unknown environments; comparison against daily Traffic data.

**Excluded:** inferring unique humans from unique-cloner counts; treating API/file reads or archive downloads as full clones; inferring worker intent from missing check-ins; assigning IP identity or credential stability without evidence; treating every worker turn as a new cloud environment.

## Current verified state

- Issue #1315 remains open with four comments at the current readback. The shared log now contains 19/19 evidence-bounded ring-label dispositions: 17 reconstructed entries and two coordinator UNAVAILABLE/UNKNOWN current-thread dispositions (Elias Kern and Ravel). The append-only ledger now has 67 rows: 51 checkout-materialization-classified rows, 15 `CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE`, and 1 `POSSIBLE FULL CLONE — MECHANISM UNKNOWN`; six rows are explicit revisions and do not count as additional checkout events. Eight new HsH checkout event rows were appended, with six `SHALLOW_1` and two `FULL_HISTORY` materializations. Five checkout heads matched run heads; three explicit-main checkouts were ahead by one or three commits. - Historical traffic reference: the supplied 14-day window had 48,880 clones and 4,686 unique cloners; an earlier daily series covered Oct 19-Nov 1. These are user-supplied dashboard readings, not recomputed in this action plan.

Status: ACTIVE STANDING PROVENANCE CONTROL
Effective: 2026-09-23
Owner: project-wide; any instance/system learning of repository provisioning should append or revise evidence.

## Principle
Record repository-copy/provisioning events even when the mechanism is unknown. Repository presence does not imply a clone. API/connector access, fetch, pull, actions/checkout, archive download, and browser access are not full clones unless evidence establishes GitHub Traffic would count them as such.

## Required classifications
- CONFIRMED FULL CLONE
- CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE
- POSSIBLE FULL CLONE — MECHANISM UNKNOWN
- REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN
- NO EVIDENCE OF REPOSITORY ACCESS

## Required fields
event_id, timestamp, timestamp_precision, actor_system, repository, environment_id, operation, mechanism, fresh_environment, traffic_clone_expected, classification, evidence, purpose, related_id, confidence, prior_classification, revision_reason.

Mechanism vocabulary: git clone; shallow clone; fetch; pull; actions/checkout; API/connector; archive download; cached workspace; unknown provisioning; other.

traffic_clone_expected: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.
fresh_environment: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.

## Revision rule
Never erase an earlier UNKNOWN classification. When later evidence resolves an event, preserve prior_classification and revision_reason.

## Retention
This ledger is provenance infrastructure and is not disposable run-log material. Before shorter-lived operational logs expire, retain identifiers, timestamps, mechanism classification, evidentiary summary, and retained-artifact pointers here.

## Aggregation
Aggregate by repository, UTC/local date as appropriate, actor/system, confirmed full clones, possible full clones, confirmed non-clone access, and unknown provisioning events.

## Fresh cloud/Codex rule
If a fresh Codex/cloud workspace is encountered with the repository already present but provisioning mechanism is not evidenced, record REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN. Do not infer git clone.


## Actions API enumeration and checkout-materialization axes (2026-11-15)

### Run-list completeness

- Query the repository Actions run-list route with an explicit UTC `created` interval, `per_page=100`, and page number. Preserve the exact query, page number, returned count, `total_count`, and terminal-page result.
- Treat `total_count=2500` as cap-saturated and incomplete, not as an exact census. If a daily interval still returns 2500, subdivide into non-overlapping UTC hourly intervals or smaller. For each subinterval, paginate until an empty page and verify that the sum of returned page counts equals the reported count and that run IDs are unique. Use adjacent intervals with explicit boundaries; deduplicate by run ID at any inclusive boundary.
- A run with an empty Jobs API array is `NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED`; it is not proof that no checkout occurred. Preserve the run record and do not invent a checkout event.
- For each run, preserve `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `head_branch`, `head_sha`, `created_at`, `status`, and `conclusion`. For each job, preserve `job_id`, job status/conclusion, and checkout step number/name/status/conclusion.
- When `run_attempt>1`, inspect attempt-specific job records if the API exposes them. Otherwise mark attempt-history coverage incomplete; the latest run record is not a complete attempt history.

### Checkout materialization is not Traffic attribution

For each `actions/checkout` step, record the actual job-log inputs and output:

- `checkout_action` (for example, `actions/checkout@v4`)
- `checkout_ref_mode`: `EXPLICIT_MAIN`, `EXPLICIT_SHA`, `DEFAULT_EVENT_REF`, or `UNKNOWN`
- `checkout_ref` when explicit
- `checkout_depth`: numeric `fetch-depth`, when logged
- `checkout_head_sha`: the actual `git log -1 --format=%H` output after checkout
- `run_head_sha`: the Actions run object's event/head SHA
- `head_sha_match`: a comparison of those two independently sourced values, never an assumption

Use two separate classification axes:

1. `checkout_materialization`: `FULL_HISTORY` when `fetch-depth=0`; `SHALLOW_N` when a positive depth N is logged; `UNKNOWN` when not observed. This describes Git history materialized in the runner workspace.
2. `traffic_attribution`: `COUNTED`, `NOT_COUNTED`, or `UNKNOWN`. Only an authorized GitHub Traffic observation can resolve this. Checkout depth, `actions/checkout`, or a run count does not establish a Traffic clone.

When materialization is known but Traffic attribution is not, use the additive classification `CHECKOUT MATERIALIZATION KNOWN / TRAFFIC ATTRIBUTION UNKNOWN`. Keep `traffic_clone_expected` as a planning field, not an observed result. The legacy classification `CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE` must not be interpreted as `checkout_materialization=NONE`; older rows lacking the new fields are UNKNOWN on the materialization axis unless supplemented.

Optional structured fields for new Actions rows: `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `job_id`, `step_number`, `step_name`, `checkout_action`, `checkout_ref_mode`, `checkout_ref`, `checkout_depth`, `checkout_materialization`, `run_head_sha`, `checkout_head_sha`, `head_sha_match`, and `traffic_attribution`.

### Append-only supplements and aggregation

- If later job-log evidence resolves checkout depth or SHA for an existing event, append a supplement row with `is_revision=true`, `revision_of=<exact prior event_id>`, `prior_classification`, and `revision_reason`. Do not erase or rewrite the prior event.
- Aggregate checkout events by the unique key `(repository, run_id, run_attempt, job_id, step_number)`. A supplement/revision row is not a second checkout event.

### h853:s3 validation sample

- SAT archive, 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-14: 33 run records on page 1 and 0 on page 2. The 27 previously uninspected runs were examined at job level. Across all 33 runs: 23 checkout jobs and 10 failed FLC test runs with no job records returned. All 33 report `run_attempt=1`.
- The 23 checkout jobs comprise 13 `fetch-depth=0` full-history checkouts and 10 `fetch-depth=2` shallow checkouts. All 23 job logs expose `git log -1 --format=%H`; each checked-out SHA matches the Actions run `head_sha`.
- HsH week and daily run-list queries returned the 2500 cap. Tested hourly buckets were complete: 2026-11-14 23:00-23:59:59Z returned 185 runs (100 + 85 + 0); 13:00-13:59:59Z returned 257 (100 + 100 + 57 + 0). These are method tests, not a completed HsH week census.
- The connector rejected `/traffic/clones?per=day` and `/traffic/views?per=day` as unsupported URL routes. This is a connector-route limitation, not evidence of GitHub permission denial. No Traffic count is claimed.


### Compact Jobs API step-summary omission guard (2026-11-19)

- A compact `actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` response can return a job record while omitting its step details. An empty or missing `steps` field in that compact response is not evidence that the job had no checkout.
- After job enumeration, use the dedicated workflow-job-steps endpoint and decoded job logs to establish checkout step number/name/status, action, explicit ref, `fetch-depth`, and the actual post-checkout `git log -1 --format=%H` value. Record which source supports each field.
- If the dedicated step endpoint and job log disagree, preserve UNKNOWN and investigate; do not infer a negative checkout observation from a compact summary.
- Counterexample: the two `Maintain H(s)H navigation` jobs #43747347981 and #43747508618 in the 2026-11-15 18:30-18:39:59Z partition had successful step-2 checkouts (`fetch-depth=0`) despite the compact Jobs API summary omitting their step details. The h917:s2 report's four-checkout count is corrected additively; two missing rows were appended, with no prior ledger row rewritten.


## Run-list snapshot retention and job-fan-out gate | 2026-11-19

A completed run-list query is not a durable job-level work queue unless its complete response, or a lossless compact run index, is retained and independently read back before job fan-out.

Required snapshot fields:

- Repository, exact UTC query interval, endpoint and query parameters, per_page, page numbers, returned counts, total_count, terminal-page result, retrieval timestamp, and SHA-256 for each raw page or the complete response.
- For every returned run: run_id, run_attempt, workflow_id, created_at, head_sha, head_branch, event, status, and conclusion.
- Preserve raw page JSON or a lossless ordered index. Verify the stored bytes and digest before treating the enumeration as a recoverable queue.
- Bind every subsequent Jobs API result to its exact run_id and run_attempt. NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED is valid only after that exact job endpoint has actually been queried.

If the original response and complete run-ID index are absent, record RUN_ID_SNAPSHOT_NOT_RETAINED, preserve the partition cursor, and recover the source snapshot if possible. Do not silently repeat an already-completed census query. A replacement query requires explicit, documented authorization and must be distinguished from the original enumeration.

[L2]   "content": "# SAT/H(s)H Clone Ledger

Status: ACTIVE STANDING PROVENANCE CONTROL
Effective: 2026-09-23
Owner: project-wide; any instance/system learning of repository provisioning should append or revise evidence.

## Principle
Record repository-copy/provisioning events even when the mechanism is unknown. Repository presence does not imply a clone. API/connector access, fetch, pull, actions/checkout, archive download, and browser access are not full clones unless evidence establishes GitHub Traffic would count them as such.

## Required classifications
- CONFIRMED FULL CLONE
- CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE
- POSSIBLE FULL CLONE — MECHANISM UNKNOWN
- REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN
- NO EVIDENCE OF REPOSITORY ACCESS

## Required fields
event_id, timestamp, timestamp_precision, actor_system, repository, environment_id, operation, mechanism, fresh_environment, traffic_clone_expected, classification, evidence, purpose, related_id, confidence, prior_classification, revision_reason.

Mechanism vocabulary: git clone; shallow clone; fetch; pull; actions/checkout; API/connector; archive download; cached workspace; unknown provisioning; other.

traffic_clone_expected: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.
fresh_environment: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.

## Revision rule
Never erase an earlier UNKNOWN classification. When later evidence resolves an event, preserve prior_classification and revision_reason.

## Retention
This ledger is provenance infrastructure and is not disposable run-log material. Before shorter-lived operational logs expire, retain identifiers, timestamps, mechanism classification, evidentiary summary, and retained-artifact pointers here.

## Aggregation
Aggregate by repository, UTC/local date as appropriate, actor/system, confirmed full clones, possible full clones, confirmed non-clone access, and unknown provisioning events.

## Fresh cloud/Codex rule
If a fresh Codex/cloud workspace is encountered with the repository already present but provisioning mechanism is not evidenced, record REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN. Do not infer git clone.


## Actions API enumeration and checkout-materialization axes (2026-11-15)

### Run-list completeness

- Query the repository Actions run-list route with an explicit UTC `created` interval, `per_page=100`, and page number. Preserve the exact query, page number, returned count, `total_count`, and terminal-page result.
- Treat `total_count=2500` as cap-saturated and incomplete, not as an exact census. If a daily interval still returns 2500, subdivide into non-overlapping UTC hourly intervals or smaller. For each subinterval, paginate until an empty page and verify that the sum of returned page counts equals the reported count and that run IDs are unique. Use adjacent intervals with explicit boundaries; deduplicate by run ID at any inclusive boundary.
- A run with an empty Jobs API array is `NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED`; it is not proof that no checkout occurred. Preserve the run record and do not invent a checkout event.
- For each run, preserve `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `head_branch`, `head_sha`, `created_at`, `status`, and `conclusion`. For each job, preserve `job_id`, job status/conclusion, and checkout step number/name/status/conclusion.
- When `run_attempt>1`, inspect attempt-specific job records if the API exposes them. Otherwise mark attempt-history coverage incomplete; the latest run record is not a complete attempt history.

### Checkout materialization is not Traffic attribution

For each `actions/checkout` step, record the actual job-log inputs and output:

- `checkout_action` (for example, `actions/checkout@v4`)
- `checkout_ref_mode`: `EXPLICIT_MAIN`, `EXPLICIT_SHA`, `DEFAULT_EVENT_REF`, or `UNKNOWN`
- `checkout_ref` when explicit
- `checkout_depth`: numeric `fetch-depth`, when logged
- `checkout_head_sha`: the actual `git log -1 --format=%H` output after checkout
- `run_head_sha`: the Actions run object's event/head SHA
- `head_sha_match`: a comparison of those two independently sourced values, never an assumption

Use two separate classification axes:

1. `checkout_materialization`: `FULL_HISTORY` when `fetch-depth=0`; `SHALLOW_N` when a positive depth N is logged; `UNKNOWN` when not observed. This describes Git history materialized in the runner workspace.
2. `traffic_attribution`: `COUNTED`, `NOT_COUNTED`, or `UNKNOWN`. Only an authorized GitHub Traffic observation can resolve this. Checkout depth, `actions/checkout`, or a run count does not establish a Traffic clone.

When materialization is known but Traffic attribution is not, use the additive classification `CHECKOUT MATERIALIZATION KNOWN / TRAFFIC ATTRIBUTION UNKNOWN`. Keep `traffic_clone_expected` as a planning field, not an observed result. The legacy classification `CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE` must not be interpreted as `checkout_materialization=NONE`; older rows lacking the new fields are UNKNOWN on the materialization axis unless supplemented.

Optional structured fields for new Actions rows: `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `job_id`, `step_number`, `step_name`, `checkout_action`, `checkout_ref_mode`, `checkout_ref`, `checkout_depth`, `checkout_materialization`, `run_head_sha`, `checkout_head_sha`, `head_sha_match`, and `traffic_attribution`.

### Append-only supplements and aggregation

- If later job-log evidence resolves checkout depth or SHA for an existing event, append a supplement row with `is_revision=true`, `revision_of=<exact prior event_id>`, `prior_classification`, and `revision_reason`. Do not erase or rewrite the prior event.
- Aggregate checkout events by the unique key `(repository, run_id, run_attempt, job_id, step_number)`. A supplement/revision row is not a second checkout event.

### h853:s3 validation sample

- SAT archive, 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-14: 33 run records on page 1 and 0 on page 2. The 27 previously uninspected runs were examined at job level. Across all 33 runs: 23 checkout jobs and 10 failed FLC test runs with no job records returned. All 33 report `run_attempt=1`.
- The 23 checkout jobs comprise 13 `fetch-depth=0` full-history checkouts and 10 `fetch-depth=2` shallow checkouts. All 23 job logs expose `git log -1 --format=%H`; each checked-out SHA matches the Actions run `head_sha`.
- HsH week and daily run-list queries returned the 2500 cap. Tested hourly buckets were complete: 2026-11-14 23:00-23:59:59Z returned 185 runs (100 + 85 + 0); 13:00-13:59:59Z returned 257 (100 + 100 + 57 + 0). These are method tests, not a completed HsH week census.
- The connector rejected `/traffic/clones?per=day` and `/traffic/views?per=day` as unsupported URL routes. This is a connector-route limitation, not evidence of GitHub permission denial. No Traffic count is claimed.


### Compact Jobs API step-summary omission guard (2026-11-19)

- A compact `actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` response can return a job record while omitting its step details. An empty or missing `steps` field in that compact response is not evidence that the job had no checkout.
- After job enumeration, use the dedicated workflow-job-steps endpoint and decoded job logs to establish checkout step number/name/status, action, explicit ref, `fetch-depth`, and the actual post-checkout `git log -1 --format=%H` value. Record which source supports each field.
- If the dedicated step endpoint and job log disagree, preserve UNKNOWN and investigate; do not infer a negative checkout observation from a compact summary.
- Counterexample: the two `Maintain H(s)H navigation` jobs #43747347981 and #43747508618 in the 2026-11-15 18:30-18:39:59Z partition had successful step-2 checkouts (`fetch-depth=0`) despite the compact Jobs API summary omitting their step details. The h917:s2 report's four-checkout count is corrected additively; two missing rows were appended, with no prior ledger row rewritten.


## Run-list snapshot retention and job-fan-out gate | 2026-11-19

A completed run-list query is not a durable job-level work queue unless its complete response, or a lossless compact run index, is retained and independently read back before job fan-out.

Required snapshot fields:

- Repository, exact UTC query interval, endpoint and query parameters, per_page, page numbers, returned counts, total_count, terminal-page result, retrieval timestamp, and SHA-256 for each raw page or the complete response.
- For every returned run: run_id, run_attempt, workflow_id, created_at, head_sha, head_branch, event, status, and conclusion.
- Preserve raw page JSON or a lossless ordered index. Verify the stored bytes and digest before treating the enumeration as a recoverable queue.
- Bind every subsequent Jobs API result to its exact run_id and run_attempt. NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED is valid only after that exact job endpoint has actually been queried.

If the original response and complete run-ID index are absent, record RUN_ID_SNAPSHOT_NOT_RETAINED, preserve the partition cursor, and recover the source snapshot if possible. Do not silently repeat an already-completed census query. A replacement query requires explicit, documented authorization and must be distinguished from the original enumeration.

Primary Workflow Health is part of the primary workflow, not an occasional side project. Every actual worker activation checks whether the machinery needed to do its work is functioning, whether previously observed failures have been diagnosed, and whether unfinished maintenance has a durable pickup route.

This queue is persistent. If an item cannot be completed in the current activation, update its exact status, evidence, owner/coordination lane, smallest next action, dependencies, review trigger and return route. The next eligible activation picks up the highest-priority unblocked item without duplicating work or displacing protected P0/P1 commitments.

## Standing per-activation health check

1. Read the current workflow orientation, Steering Charter, live task graph, selected worker continuity/current-work record, relevant open issues and recent canonical receipts/handoffs.
2. Check relay health: enabled task IDs/schedules/phases unchanged; task graph node/edge counts and reachability; task-to-owner/next-cursor consistency; run/receipt/publisher/readback state; failed/cancelled/pending workflows; stale pointers; orphaned or blocked work.
